newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebels say they 50 km from southern city.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels say they 50 km from southern city.

text.p: Sudanese rebels said on Saturday they were only about 50 km (30 miles) from the southern city of Juba and they were certain to capture it.
At the end of a four-day meeting of leaders of the Sudanese opposition, Commander Deng Alor Koul of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) however said he could not say when Juba would fall.
"Juba is our military objective. We are now approximately 30 miles (50 km) from Juba. We cannot give a time frame, but we are certain we will take Juba," he told reporters in the Eritrean capital.

Following a visit this week by foreign journalists to parts of southern Sudan recently captured by rebels, Sudan's First Vice President Al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh was quoted on Saturday as denying that rebels had seized contested areas in the south.
The Sudan al-Hadith newspaper quoted Saleh as saying rebel claims that they have captured southern positions were "mere allegations" and that Khartoum's army was in "full control".

In what is seen by some diplomats as the most successful rebel offensive since 1983, the SPLA has seized territory in the east since January and in the south this month including the major southern town of Yei and much of the road north to Juba.
Khartoum accuses Uganda, Eritrea and Ethiopia of sending troops into Sudan to fight alongside the rebels. The three countries have denied any involvement in the civil war.

In a statement at the end of their meeting, the leaders of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), a coalition of Sudanese opposition groups, said they had decided on preparations for an interim period after the Khartoum government was overthrown.
Former prime minister Sadiq al-Mahdi, who fled to Asmara from Khartoum in December, attended the meeting, which also decided to tighten coordination among the rebel forces.
The statement said NDA leaders would support popular movements inside Sudan, appeal to Sudanese outside the country and strengthen NDA radio as a tool for mobilisation.
The NDA said it wanted a boycott of government institutions outside Sudan and would launch a diplomatic offensive within three months to increase international isolation of Khartoum.
It said countries and individuals who supported the Sudanese government were attacking Sudan's people and companies investing in Sudan would be considered as legitimate military targets.

The SPLA has been fighting since 1983 for greater autonomy or independence of the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arabised north. The NDA says it wants to trigger a popular uprising in Khartoum against the Islamist government.
